summary: This bill requires the Treasury to mint and sell up to 50,000 $5 gold coins, 400,000 $1 silver coins, and 750,000 half-dollar coins in 2027 featuring Roberto Clemente, with surcharges paid to the Roberto Clemente Foundation after costs are recovered.

scores.thoughts: The bill authorizes minting of commemorative coins with strict financial assurances that the program will result in no net cost to the government (section 8). Surcharges cover all design, production, and distribution expenses. This is a standard self-funding commemorative coin program with no expansion or reduction of government spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax rates, tax policy, or revenue collection mechanisms.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms or gun regulations.
The bill contains no provisions related to immigration policy or border enforcement.
The bill contains no provisions related to abortion or reproductive rights.
The bill contains no provisions related to military or defense spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to environmental regulations or climate policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to welfare programs or social safety net policies.

Surcharges are directed in part to educational programs via the Roberto Clemente Foundation, but this is incidental to a commemorative coin program and does not alter federal education policy or funding structures.
The bill contains no provisions related to drug enforcement or decriminalization.
The bill contains no provisions related to criminal justice, sentencing, or policing.
The bill contains no provisions related to trade, tariffs, or globalization.

Section 8 explicitly requires that the program incur no net cost to the government and that all expenses be recovered before any surcharges are disbursed. This is a neutral, cost-recovery measure rather than an active policy on deficit spending or debt reduction.
The bill contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections.
The bill contains no provisions altering U.S. foreign aid policy; historical references to Clemente's personal humanitarian efforts do not constitute legislative action on foreign aid.
The bill contains no provisions related to voting access or election integrity.
The bill contains no provisions related to technology regulation or data privacy.
The findings note Clemente's historical role as a union leader, but the bill itself enacts no changes to labor law, union rights, or employer policies.
The bill contains no provisions related to religious exemptions or anti-discrimination law.
